1. Methodological positioning of the review and support for factual statements
We fully agree. In the revised manuscript we have clarified, at a higher level of prominence,
that the paper is an integrative theoretical synthesis rather than an exhaustive mapping or a
formal “systematic review” in the strict PRISMA sense. As follows:
Abstract (methodological positioning): We added an explicit statement positioning
the article as an integrative theoretical synthesis and clarifying that it combines a
structured search and thematic synthesis without claiming exhaustive coverage.
Methodological approach (early signposting): We added a short “positioning”
subsection that explains the rationale for an integrative synthesis in relation to model
construction and conceptual re-organization.
Supporting methodological references: To avoid reliance on authorial assertion, we
incorporated established methodological sources on integrative/theoretical reviews
and review typologies, which justify the approach adopted.
Because the main contribution of the manuscript is conceptual (i.e., the construction and
articulation of an interdependent model linking teacher knowledge and teacher identity), an
integrative theoretical synthesis is the most appropriate methodological form. The revised
wording is intended to align the reader’s expectations with the actual goals and procedures
of the review.

3. About the assessment of the discussion in the context of the literature
We acknowledge this evaluation and have revised the manuscript to ensure that the
intended goal is explicit: the article is an integrative synthesis aimed at conceptual model
construction rather than an exhaustive mapping of all perspectives. To address the
underlying concern, we (i) strengthened the scope statement and delimitations, and (ii)
clarified the methodological positioning so that the manuscript is assessed against the
